To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

fetal implants of IC tissue into the contralateral IC lesioned rats can ameliorate the retrieval of a previously acquired CTA, but only if the implantation is performed 45 days after IC lesions, and the recovery of the CTA learning ability is observed if NGF is administered at the time of IC lesions.
fetal brain implants in the IC ameliorate the retrieval of learned taste aversion in IC lesioned rats, but the recovery of learning abilities requires NGF supplementation.

the long-term retrieval deficits of learned aversions in rats with IC lesions can be ameliorated by fetal brain implants, but not by the implantation of other brain tissues, such as cerebellar cortex or striatum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the recovery of memory function after brain injury, and the mechanisms that underlie this process.
understanding the mechanisms underlying the effects of fetal brain implants in brain-lesioned rats.
the mechanisms that regulate the recovery of brain functions after lesions in adult rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IC lesion impairs memory for CTA and IA, but that fetal brain implants in the IC can restore memory retrieval for both tasks.
IC fetal implants are not effective in restoring the memory retrieval for learned CTAs, but are effective in restoring the ability to learn a new CTA.
fetal cortical implants in the IC are capable of inducing recovery of memory functions for learned taste aversions and inhibitory avoidance learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IC lesions produce memory deficits that are reversible with cortical implants, and that NGF is a key factor in this recovery.
the fetal cortical implants in the IC lesioned rats are able to recover the memory for a CTA and IA learning, and that the recovery of memory retrieval is a slower process than that for learning.
the brain mechanisms of learning and memory are independent, and that memory deficits can be recovered by brain implants, whereas learning deficits are irreversible.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fetal brain implants can be used to recover the memory retrieval deficits induced by IC lesions.
the fetal brain implants can be used to restore the memory for previously learned CTAs in IC lesioned rats.

fetal brain implants in IC lesioned rats can recover retrieval of previously learned taste aversion memories, and the recovery of learning abilities is dependent on the type of implant, the type of memory, and the time after the IC lesion.
